q: Choose the correct form: She ___ in a bank.
correct: works
why: With *he, she* and *it* we add *-s* to the verb: *she works.*

wrong_why.work: Careful: *she* is third person singular, so the verb needs *-s.*

why_lv: Ar *he, she* un *it* darbības vārdam pievieno *-s*: *she works*.

wrong_why_lv.work: Uzmanīgi: *she* ir 3. persona vienskaitlī, tāpēc darbības vārdam vajag *-s*.

q: Which sentence is about a habit (something you do again and again)?
correct: I drink tea every morning.
why: *Every morning* shows a habit. We use the present simple for habits and routines.
why_lv: *Every morning* rāda ieradumu. Ieradumiem un ikdienas rutīnai lieto Present Simple.

q: Use the present simple: My brother ___ football. (not / like)
answers: doesn't like
does not like
why: With *he, she, it* we use *doesn't* + the base verb: *he doesn't like.*
hints: After *doesn't* we use the base verb: *like*, not *likes.*
why_lv: Ar *he, she, it* lieto *doesn't* + darbības vārda pamatforma: *he doesn't like*.

q: Make it negative: They play tennis on Sundays.
answers: They don't play tennis on Sundays.
They do not play tennis on Sundays.
On sundays they don't play tennis.
On sundays they do not play tennis.
why: With *I, you, we, they* we make the negative with *don't* + base verb.
why_lv: Ar *I, you, we, they* noliegumu veido ar *don't* + pamatforma.

q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct: She don't work on Sunday.
why: With *she* we say *doesn't*: *She doesn't work on Sunday.*
why_lv: Ar *she* saka *doesn't*: *She doesn't work on Sunday.*

q: Is this sentence correct? 'Does he works here?'
correct: No. It should be 'Does he work here?'
wrong: No. It should be 'Do he works here?'
No. It should be 'Is he works here?'
why: After *does* we use the base verb: *work*, not *works.* *Does he work here?*
why_lv: Pēc *does* lieto pamatformu: *work*, nevis *works*. *Does he work here?*

q: Write one sentence about a daily habit of your friend or colleague. Start with He or She and use an action verb in the present simple (for example, works, goes or has breakfast).
must: Use *He* or *She* with a present-simple verb, such as *works*, *goes* or *has*.
Lieto *He* vai *She* ar darbības vārdu Present Simple, piemēram, *works*, *goes* vai *has*.
model: She starts work at eight every day.
why: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
why_lv: Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

q: Choose the correct word: Where ___ your sister work?
correct: does
why: Questions in the present simple: *do/does* + subject + base verb. *Sister* = *she*, so *does.*
why_lv: Jautājumi Present Simple: *do/does* + teik. priekšmets + pamatforma. *Sister = she*, tāpēc *does*.

q: Which sentence is about a timetable?
correct: The train leaves at 7.45 tomorrow.
why: We use the present simple for fixed timetables, even for the future.
why_lv: Fiksētiem sarakstiem un grafikiem lieto Present Simple, pat runājot par nākotni.

q: What time ___ the film usually ___? (start)
answers: does
start
why: Question: *What time* + *does* + subject + base verb.
hints: After *does* we use the base verb: *start*, not *starts.*
why_lv: Jautājums: *What time + does* + teik. priekšmets + pamatforma.

q: Make a question with How: She goes to work by bus.
answers: How does she go to work?
How does she get to work?
How does she travel to work?
why: Question: *How* + *does* + *she* + base verb. The *-es* goes away: *goes* becomes *go.*
hints: After *does* use the base verb: *go*, not *goes.*
why_lv: Jautājums: *How + does + she* + pamatforma. Galotne *-es* pazūd: *goes* kļūst par *go*.

q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct: Do they speaks English?
why: After *do* we need the base verb: *Do they speak English?*
why_lv: Pēc *do* vajag pamatformu: *Do they speak English?*

q: Choose the correct option.
correct: He goes to the gym on Mondays.
wrong: He go to the gym on Mondays.
He is go to the gym on Mondays.
He going to the gym on Mondays.
why: With *he, she, it* the present simple verb takes *-s* or *-es*: *he goes.*
why_lv: Ar *he, she, it* darbības vārdam Present Simple pievieno *-s* vai *-es*: *he goes*.

q: Write a question to ask a new colleague about their free time. Start with Do you or What do you.
must: ^\s*(do|what do|where do|when do|how often do|who do)\s+you\b
Start with *Do you ...* or *What do you ...*
Sāc ar *Do you* ... vai *What do you* ...
End the question with a question mark.
model: What do you usually do at the weekend?
why: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
why_lv: Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

q: Which verb is normally NOT used in a continuous tense when it describes a state of knowledge?
correct: know
why: When *know* describes knowledge, we normally use a simple tense: *I know the answer*, not *I am knowing the answer*.
why_lv: Ja *know* apzīmē zināšanas, parasti lieto vienkāršo laiku: *I know the answer*, nevis *I am knowing the answer*.

q: Which sentence states a general fact?
correct: The Earth orbits the Sun.
why: Use the present simple for general facts and regular processes: *The Earth orbits the Sun.*
why_lv: Vispārīgiem faktiem un regulāriem procesiem lieto Present Simple: *The Earth orbits the Sun.*

q: Use the present simple for a timetable: Our flight ___ at 6.40 tomorrow morning. (leave)
answers: leaves
why: The present simple is used for timetables, even for the future: *the flight leaves.*
why_lv: Grafikiem lieto Present Simple, pat runājot par nākotni: *the flight leaves*.

q: Make it negative and use 'any': She has money.
answers: She doesn't have any money.
She does not have any money.
She hasn't any money.
She has not any money.
why: Negative: *doesn't* + base verb. With *any* for uncountable or plural nouns.
why_lv: Noliegums: *doesn't* + pamatforma. Ar *any* pie neskaitāmiem vai daudzskaitļa lietvārdiem.

q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct: My brother is owning a small shop.
why: *Own* is a state verb, so we use the present simple: *My brother owns a small shop.*
why_lv: *Own* ir stāvokļa darbības vārds, tāpēc lieto Present Simple: *My brother owns a small shop.*

q: Choose the correct option.
correct: 'I want a coffee.'
why: State verbs (*want, need, like, know*) are normally not used in the continuous.
why_lv: Stāvokļa darbības vārdus (*want, need, like, know*) parasti nelieto Continuous formā.

q: Write two sentences about a timetable, for example a train, a class or a shop. Use the present simple with a time, as in: The train leaves at 7.45.
must: Use a timetable verb with *at* and a time, such as *at nine*, *at 9.00* or *at noon*.
Lieto grafika darbības vārdu ar *at* un laiku, piemēram, *at nine*, *at 9.00* vai *at noon*.
model: My class starts at 9.00. It finishes at 11.30.
why: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
why_lv: Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

q: Look! The children ___ in the garden.
correct: are playing
why: Right now: *am/is/are* + verb-ing. *The children* = *they*, so *are playing.*
why_lv: Tieši tagad: *am/is/are* + darbības vārds ar *-ing*. *The children* = *they*, tāpēc *are playing*.

q: Which sentence is happening right now?
correct: I'm cooking dinner.
why: The present continuous shows an action in progress now.
why_lv: Present Continuous rāda darbību, kas notiek tieši tagad.

q: Shh! The baby ___. (sleep)
answers: is sleeping
why: Now: *is + sleeping.* *The baby* = *it.*
hints: For an action happening now we use *is* + verb-ing: *is sleeping.*
Darbībai, kas notiek tagad, lieto *is* + darbības vārds ar *-ing*: *is sleeping*.
why_lv: Tagad: *is + sleeping*. *The baby = it.*

q: She ___ in the park now. (run)
answers: is running
why: Spelling: *run* becomes *running* (we double the *n*).
hints: Short verbs with one vowel + one consonant double the last letter: *running.*
Īsiem darbības vārdiem ar vienu patskani un vienu līdzskani dubulto pēdējo burtu: *running*.
why_lv: Pareizrakstība: *run* kļūst par *running* (dubulto *n*).

q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct: They are play football.
why: After *are* we need verb-ing: *They are playing football.*
why_lv: Pēc *are* vajag darbības vārdu ar *-ing*: *They are playing football.*

q: A friend is at the station and you ask about now. Choose the correct option.
correct: What are you doing now?
why: For right now we use *are* + *you* + verb-ing.
why_lv: Jautājumam par tagadni lieto *are + you* + darbības vārds ar *-ing*.

q: Look around you. Write one sentence about what you are doing now. Start with I am.
must: Use *I am* (or *I'm*) + verb-ing, for example: *I am sitting at my desk.*
Lieto *I am* (vai *I'm*) + darbības vārds ar *-ing*, piemēram: *I am sitting at my desk.*
model: I am sitting at my desk.
why: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
why_lv: Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

q: My brother ___ for an exam this week, so he is very busy.
correct: is studying
why: A temporary situation around now: *am/is/are* + verb-ing.
why_lv: Pagaidu situācija šobrīd: *am/is/are* + darbības vārds ar *-ing*.

q: Which sentence is about a plan for the future?
correct: I'm meeting Anna tomorrow at five.
why: The present continuous with a future time word shows a fixed plan.
why_lv: Present Continuous ar nākotnes laika vārdu rāda fiksētu plānu.

q: Ask about a future arrangement. Use the present continuous: What ___ you ___ this weekend? (do)
answers: are
doing
why: Question: *What* + *are* + *you* + verb-ing.
why_lv: Jautājums: *What + are + you* + darbības vārds ar *-ing*.

q: Make it negative: They are waiting for the bus.
answers: They aren't waiting for the bus.
They are not waiting for the bus.
why: Negative: *am/is/are* + *not* + verb-ing.
why_lv: Noliegums: *am/is/are + not* + darbības vārds ar *-ing*.

q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct: She is have a shower.
wrong: Are you coming to the party?
why: After *is* we need verb-ing: *She is having a shower.*
why_lv: Pēc *is* vajag darbības vārdu ar *-ing*: *She is having a shower.*

q: You are staying in Riga temporarily for one month. Which sentence best emphasises your temporary situation now?
correct: I'm living in a small flat this month.
wrong: I live in a small flat this month.
I lived in a small flat this month.
I will living in a small flat.
why: The continuous shows a temporary situation.
why_lv: Continuous rāda pagaidu situāciju.

q: Write a question to ask a friend about their plans for tonight. Use Are you + verb-ing.
must: Use *Are you* + verb-ing, for example: *Are you going out tonight?*
Lieto *Are you* + darbības vārds ar *-ing*, piemēram: *Are you going out tonight?*
End the question with a question mark.
model: Are you going out tonight?
why: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
why_lv: Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

q: Please be quiet. I ___ to concentrate.
correct: am trying
why: An action in progress at the moment of speaking: *am* + verb-ing.
why_lv: Darbība, kas notiek runāšanas brīdī: *am* + darbības vārds ar *-ing*.

q: Which sentence describes a change that is happening now?
correct: The weather is getting colder.
wrong: The weather is cold in winter.
It gets cold in winter every year.
why: We use the present continuous for changes in progress: *getting colder, growing, rising.*
why_lv: Izmaiņām, kas notiek tagad, lieto Present Continuous: *getting colder, growing, rising*.

q: Use the present continuous: These days more people ___ from home. (work)
answers: are working
why: A trend around now: *are* + verb-ing.
why_lv: Tendence mūsdienās: *are* + darbības vārds ar *-ing*.

q: Make a question with Why: He is shouting.
answers: Why is he shouting?
why: Question word + *is* + subject + verb-ing.
why_lv: Jautājamais vārds + *is* + teik. priekšmets + darbības vārds ar *-ing*.

q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct: She is wanting a new phone.
wrong: I'm having a great time here.
why: *Want* is a state verb, so we use the present simple: *She wants a new phone.*
why_lv: *Want* ir stāvokļa darbības vārds, tāpēc lieto Present Simple: *She wants a new phone.*

q: Is this statement true? 'I'm living with my parents at the moment' sounds more temporary than 'I live with my parents.'
correct: Yes, it is true.
wrong: No. They mean exactly the same.
No. Only 'live' can show a temporary situation.
why: The present continuous often shows that something is temporary or changing.
why_lv: Present Continuous bieži rāda, ka kaut kas ir pagaidu vai mainās.

q: Write one sentence about a change in your life or your city these days. Use the present continuous.
model: More people are working from home these days.
why: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
why_lv: Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

q: Yesterday I ___ to the cinema.
correct: went
why: *Go* is irregular. The past form is *went.*
why_lv: *Go* ir neregulārs darbības vārds. Tā pagātnes forma ir *went*.

q: Which sentence is about something finished in the past?
correct: We visited Rome last year.
why: *Last year* is a finished time. We use the past simple.
why_lv: *Last year* ir pabeigts laiks. Lieto Past Simple.

q: She ___ TV last night. (not / watch)
answers: didn't watch
did not watch
why: Negative past simple: *didn't* + base verb.
hints: After *didn't* we use the base verb: *watch*, not *watched.*
why_lv: Noliegums Past Simple: *didn't* + darbības vārda pamatforma.

q: Make a question: He played football.
answers: Did he play football?
why: Question: *Did* + subject + base verb.
hints: After *did* we use the base verb: *play*, not *played.*
why_lv: Jautājums: *Did* + teik. priekšmets + pamatforma.

q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct: I didn't went to school.
why: After *didn't* use the base verb: *I didn't go to school.*
why_lv: Pēc *didn't* lieto pamatformu: *I didn't go to school.*

q: Is this sentence correct? 'I buyed a new phone yesterday.'
correct: No. It should be 'I bought a new phone yesterday.'
wrong: No. It should be 'I buy a new phone yesterday.'
No. It should be 'I did bought a new phone yesterday.'
why: *Buy* is an irregular verb. The past form is *bought*, not *buyed.*
why_lv: *Buy* ir neregulārs darbības vārds. Pagātnes forma ir *bought*, nevis *buyed*.

q: Write one sentence about what you did yesterday. Use a past verb and the word yesterday.
must: Use a verb in the past (for example: *met, went, worked*).
Lieto darbības vārdu pagātnē (piemēram, *met, went, worked*).
model: Yesterday I met a friend for coffee.
why: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
why_lv: Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

q: Where ___ you ___ last summer?
correct: did ... go
why: Past simple questions: *did* + subject + base verb.
why_lv: Jautājumi Past Simple: *did* + teik. priekšmets + pamatforma.

q: Which words usually go with the past simple?
correct: yesterday, last week, three days ago
wrong: now, at the moment, these days
why: Finished time words (*yesterday, last week, ago*) go with the past simple.
why_lv: Pabeigta laika vārdi (*yesterday, last week, ago*) der kopā ar Past Simple.

q: We ___ late because the bus ___ slow. (be)
answers: were
was
why: *Be* in the past: *I/he/she/it was, you/we/they were.*
why_lv: *Be* pagātnē: *I/he/she/it was, you/we/they were.*

q: Yesterday he ___ at 7 and ___ a shower. (wake up / have)
answers: woke up
had
why: Both verbs are irregular: *wake - woke, have - had.*
why_lv: Abi darbības vārdi ir neregulāri: *wake - woke, have - had*.

q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct: Did you saw the match?
wrong: I met her two years ago.
why: After *did* we use the base verb: *Did you see the match?*
why_lv: Pēc *did* lieto pamatformu: *Did you see the match?*

q: A colleague asks: 'What did you do at the weekend?' Choose the correct option.
correct: I went hiking with my brother.
wrong: I go hiking with my brother.
I am going hiking with my brother.
I have gone hiking with my brother.
why: The question is in the past simple, so we answer about a finished time with the past simple.
why_lv: Jautājums ir Past Simple, tāpēc par pabeigtu laiku atbild ar Past Simple.

q: Write two short sentences about your last holiday or day off. Use the past simple.
must: Use verbs in the past simple (*went, stayed, visited ...*).
Lieto darbības vārdus Past Simple (*went, stayed, visited* ...).
model: I went to the sea. We swam every day.
why: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
why_lv: Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

q: Last year, they ___ married in Paris.
correct: got
why: *Get* is irregular. The past simple form is *got.*
why_lv: *Get* ir neregulārs. Past Simple forma ir *got*.

q: Which sentence uses the past simple to describe two completed actions in sequence?
correct: She opened the door and walked in.
wrong: She was opening the door and walking in.
She opens the door and walks in.
She has opened the door and has walked in.
why: We use the past simple for a series of finished actions in order.
why_lv: Pabeigtu darbību virknei secībā lieto Past Simple.

q: I ___ Tom at the party, so I called him later. (not / see)
answers: didn't see
did not see
why: Negative: *didn't* + base verb.
why_lv: Noliegums: *didn't* + pamatforma.

q: Make a question with When: She moved to London.
answers: When did she move to London?
why: Question word + *did* + subject + base verb.
hints: After *did* we use the base verb: *move.*
why_lv: Jautājamais vārds + *did* + teik. priekšmets + pamatforma.

q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct: Why did you went home early?
why: After *did* we use the base verb: *Why did you go home early?*
why_lv: Pēc *did* lieto pamatformu: *Why did you go home early?*

q: You want to say your report was finished in March. Choose the correct option.
correct: I finished it in March.
wrong: I have finished it in March.
I am finishing it in March.
why: *In March* is a finished time, so we use the past simple, not the present perfect.
why_lv: *In March* ir pabeigts laiks, tāpēc lieto Past Simple, nevis Present Perfect.

q: Write two sentences that start a story. Say what happened first and what happened next (use Then or After that).
must: Use *Then* or *After that* to show the order.
Lieto *Then* vai *After that*, lai parādītu secību.
Use verbs in the past simple.
model: I got up late. Then I missed the bus.
why: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
why_lv: Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

q: At 8 o'clock yesterday, dinner preparation was already in progress. Complete with the past continuous: I ___ dinner.
correct: was cooking
why: An action in progress at a moment in the past: *was/were* + verb-ing.
why_lv: Darbība, kas pagātnē noteiktā brīdī bija procesā: *was/were* + darbības vārds ar *-ing*.

q: Which sentence shows an action in progress at a moment in the past?
correct: At nine, she was reading in bed.
wrong: At nine, she reads in bed.
At nine, she read the book.
At nine, she has read in bed.
why: *At nine* is a moment in the past. The past continuous shows what was in progress then.
why_lv: *At nine* ir brīdis pagātnē. Past Continuous rāda, kas tad norisinājās.

q: Use the past continuous: They ___ TV when I arrived. (watch)
answers: were watching
why: *They* = *were* + verb-ing.
why_lv: *They = were* + darbības vārds ar *-ing*.

q: Use the past continuous: ___ you ___ at 6 pm? (work)
answers: Were
working
why: Question: *Were* + *you* + verb-ing.
why_lv: Jautājums: *Were + you* + darbības vārds ar *-ing*.

q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct: I was watch TV.
why: After *was/were* we need verb-ing: *I was watching TV.*
why_lv: Pēc *was/were* vajag darbības vārdu ar *-ing*: *I was watching TV.*

q: A friend asks: 'What were you doing at midnight?' Choose the correct option.
correct: I was sleeping.
why: The question uses the past continuous, so the answer also describes what was in progress.
why_lv: Jautājumā ir Past Continuous, tāpēc atbilde arī apraksta to, kas bija procesā.

q: Write a sentence about what you were doing at 7 pm yesterday. Use was/were + verb-ing.
must: Use *was* or *were* + verb-ing, for example: *I was cooking dinner.*
Lieto *was* vai *were* + darbības vārds ar *-ing*, piemēram: *I was cooking dinner.*
model: At 7 pm yesterday, I was cooking dinner.
why: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
why_lv: Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

q: Describe the action already in progress, using the past continuous: I ___ along the street when I saw an old friend.
correct: was walking
why: A longer action in progress (*was walking*) is interrupted by a short action (*saw*).
why_lv: Garāku darbību (*was walking*) pārtrauc īsa darbība (*saw*).

q: In 'When Mia called, I was cooking', which action started first?
correct: Cooking.
why: The past continuous action was already happening when the short action (*called*) happened.
why_lv: Past Continuous darbība jau notika, kad notika īsā darbība (*called*).

q: While she ___, her phone ___. (drive / ring)
answers: was driving
drove
rang
was ringing
why: Long action: *was driving.* Short action that interrupts: *rang.*
why_lv: Garā darbība: *was driving*. Īsā darbība, kas pārtrauc: *rang*.

q: It ___ when we left the house, so we took umbrellas. (rain)
answers: was raining
why: The background situation is in progress: *was raining.*
why_lv: Fona situācija bija procesā: *was raining*.

q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct: When I arrived, they was having lunch.
wrong: When I arrived, they were having lunch.
While I was reading, he was watching TV.
She was cooking when the lights went out.
why: The subject *they* needs *were*: *When I arrived, they were having lunch.* The lunch was already in progress.
why_lv: Ar *they* lieto *were*: *When I arrived, they were having lunch.* Pusdienošana jau bija sākusies.

q: You tell a story: 'I was walking home. Suddenly a dog ___ out of the garden.' Choose the correct option.
correct: ran
why: A sudden, short action that interrupts uses the past simple.
why_lv: Pēkšņai īsai darbībai, kas pārtrauc citu darbību, lieto Past Simple.

q: Write one sentence with 'when' about something that interrupted you. Use the past continuous and the past simple.
must: Use *was/were* + verb-ing for the longer action.
Garākai darbībai lieto *was/were* + darbības vārds ar *-ing*.
Use the past simple for the short action (*rang, arrived, called ...*).
Īsajai darbībai lieto Past Simple (*rang, arrived, called* ...).
model: I was cooking dinner when my friend called.
why: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
why_lv: Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

q: Choose the correct form: I ___ to call you, but my phone died.
correct: was going
why: *Was/were going to* + base verb = a plan in the past that did not happen.
why_lv: *Was/were going to* + pamatforma = plāns pagātnē, kas nenotika.

q: What does 'I was going to call you' mean?
correct: I planned to call you.
wrong: I am going to call you now.
I never wanted to call you.
why: *Was going to* describes a past intention. Context tells us whether it happened: *I was going to call, but I forgot* shows that it did not.
why_lv: *Was going to* izsaka nodomu pagātnē. Konteksts parāda, vai tas īstenojās: *I was going to call, but I forgot* nozīmē, ka zvans nenotika.

q: Sorry, I ___ to answer your email, but I was very busy. (go)
answers: was going
why: Plan in the past: *was going to* + base verb.
why_lv: Plāns pagātnē: *was going to* + pamatforma.

q: While the guests ___, the band ___ quiet music. (arrive / play)
answers: were arriving
arrived
was playing
played
why: Two actions in progress at the same time: *while* + past continuous, past continuous.
why_lv: Divas darbības, kas notiek vienlaikus: *while* + Past Continuous, Past Continuous.

q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct: They was going to meet us, but they were late.
wrong: I was going to call you, but I lost your number.
She was going to leave when he arrived.
We were going to stay longer.
why: *They* needs *were*: *They were going to meet us.*
why_lv: *They* vajag *were*: *They were going to meet us.*

q: You want to describe a plan that did not happen. Choose the correct option.
correct: We were going to travel to Italy, but we cancelled.
wrong: We are going to travel to Italy, but we cancelled.
We travel to Italy, but we cancelled.
We have travelled to Italy, but we cancelled.
why: Past tense + *but* shows the plan changed: *were going to.*
why_lv: Pagātnes forma + *but* rāda, ka plāns mainījās: *were going to*.

q: Write a sentence about a plan you had but did not do. Use was/were going to and but.
must: Use the word *but* to say what happened instead.
Lieto vārdu *but*, lai pateiktu, kas notika tā vietā.
model: I was going to go to the gym, but I was too tired.
why: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
why_lv: Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

q: I have never ___ sushi.
correct: eaten
why: Present perfect = *have/has* + past participle. The past participle of *eat* is *eaten.*
why_lv: Present Perfect = *have/has* + darbības vārda 3. forma. *Eat* 3. forma ir *eaten*.

q: Which sentence is about life experience (no exact time)?
correct: I've been to Spain.
wrong: I go to Spain every year.
why: We use the present perfect for experiences up to now when the time is not important.
why_lv: Dzīves pieredzei līdz šim brīdim lieto Present Perfect, kad precīzs laiks nav svarīgs.

q: She ___ her homework. (just / finish)
answers: has just finished
why: *Just* goes between *has/have* and the past participle: *has just finished.*
hints: After *has* we need the past participle: *finished.*
why_lv: *Just* iet starp *has/have* un 3. formu: *has just finished*.

q: I haven't ___ her yet. (call)
answers: called
why: Negative: *haven't* + past participle. *Yet* goes with the present perfect.
why_lv: Noliegums: *haven't* + 3. forma. *Yet* der kopā ar Present Perfect.

q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct: I have went to London twice.
wrong: She has lived here for years.
Have you ever tried Thai food?
We haven't seen that film yet.
why: The past participle of *go* is *gone* (or *been* for visits): *I have been to London twice.*
why_lv: *Go* 3. forma ir *gone* (apmeklējumiem *been*): *I have been to London twice.*

q: Someone asks you: 'Have you ever been to Rome?' Choose the correct option.
correct: Yes, I have.
why: Short answers repeat the helper verb of the question: *Have you ...? Yes, I have.*
why_lv: Īsā atbilde atkārto jautājuma palīgdarbības vārdu: *Have you* ...? *Yes, I have.*

q: Write one sentence about something you have never done but would like to do. Use I have never.
must: Use *I have never* + past participle, for example: *I have never been to Japan.*
Lieto *I have never* + 3. forma, piemēram: *I have never been to Japan.*
model: I have never been to Japan.
why: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
why_lv: Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

q: I've worked here ___ five years.
correct: for
why: Use *for* + a period of time (*five years*). Use *since* + a starting point (*2020*).
why_lv: *For* lieto ar laika posmu (*five years*). *Since* lieto ar sākuma brīdi (2020).

q: Which sentence means: it started in the past and is still true now?
correct: I have known Tom for ten years.
wrong: I knew Tom ten years ago.
I did know Tom for ten years.
why: The present perfect with *for/since* connects the past with now.
why_lv: Present Perfect ar *for/since* savieno pagātni ar tagadni.

q: They ___ married for 20 years. (be)
answers: have been
why: Unfinished period: *have been* + *for 20 years.*
hints: With *for/since* and a situation that continues, use the present perfect: *have been.*
Ar *for/since* un situāciju, kas turpinās, lieto Present Perfect: *have been*.
why_lv: Nebeigts laika posms: *have been + for 20 years*.

q: Make a question with How long: She has worked here since June.
answers: How long has she worked here?
How long has she been working here?
why: *How long* + *has* + subject + past participle.
why_lv: *How long + has* + teik. priekšmets + 3. forma.

q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct: I have seen him yesterday.
wrong: We have known each other for years.
why: *Yesterday* is a finished time. Use the past simple: *I saw him yesterday.*
why_lv: *Yesterday* ir pabeigts laiks. Lieto Past Simple: *I saw him yesterday.*

q: You cannot open the door because your keys are missing. Which sentence most directly presents the loss as a current problem?
correct: I've lost my keys.
why: *I have lost my keys* presents the past loss as relevant now. The past simple reports the past event; context can also connect it to a current problem.
why_lv: *I have lost my keys* uzsver pagātnes notikuma saistību ar tagadni. Past Simple apraksta pagātnes notikumu; arī to konteksts var saistīt ar pašreizējo problēmu.

q: Write two sentences about how long you have lived in your city or worked in your job. Use for in one and since in the other.
model: I have lived in Riga for ten years. I have worked here since 2020.
why: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
why_lv: Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

q: It's the first time I ___ this dish.
correct: have tried
why: After *It's the first time* we use the present perfect.
why_lv: Pēc *It's the first time* lieto Present Perfect.

q: Which sentence has a finished time word, so we must use the past simple?
correct: I saw the film last night.
wrong: I've seen the film this week.
why: *Last night* is finished, so past simple. Without a finished time we can use the present perfect.
why_lv: *Last night* ir pabeigts laiks, tāpēc Past Simple. Bez pabeigta laika var lietot Present Perfect.

q: How long ___ you ___ English? (study)
answers: have
studied
been studying
why: *How long* + *have* + *you* + past participle (or *been* + verb-ing).
why_lv: *How long + have + you* + 3. forma (vai *been* + darbības vārds ar *-ing*).

q: Use the present perfect to describe life experience: I ___ in three countries, so I speak a little of each language. (live)
answers: have lived
why: Life experience up to now: *have* + past participle.
why_lv: Dzīves pieredze līdz šim brīdim: *have* + 3. forma.

q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct: I have visited Paris in 2018.
wrong: Have you ever been to Italy?
why: *In 2018* is a finished time. Use the past simple: *I visited Paris in 2018.*
why_lv: *In 2018* ir pabeigts laiks. Lieto Past Simple: *I visited Paris in 2018.*

q: Choose the correct option.
correct: I sent the email yesterday.
wrong: I have sent the email yesterday.
I will send the email yesterday.
I was sending the email yesterday.
why: Finished time words (*yesterday, last week, in 2018*) need the past simple.
why_lv: Pabeigta laika vārdiem (*yesterday, last week, in 2018*) vajag Past Simple.

q: Write two sentences: one present perfect about a place you have visited, and one past simple with the time you went.
must: Use the present perfect in the first sentence (*have been ...*).
Pirmajā teikumā lieto Present Perfect (*have been* ...).
Give a finished time in the second sentence (*in 2022, last year, two years ago*).
Otrajā teikumā norādi pabeigtu laiku (*in 2022, last year, two years ago*).
model: I have been to Lisbon. I went there in 2022.
why: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
why_lv: Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

q: I'm tired and I am still at my desk. Use the present perfect continuous: I ___ all day.
correct: have been working
why: Present perfect continuous = *have/has been* + verb-ing. It shows an activity over a period up to now.
why_lv: Present Perfect Continuous = *have/has been* + darbības vārds ar *-ing*. Tas rāda darbību laika posmā līdz šim brīdim.

q: What does 'I've been waiting for an hour' tell us?
correct: I started waiting an hour ago. I am still waiting (or I have just stopped).
wrong: I waited for one hour last week.
I will wait for an hour.
why: The present perfect continuous shows how long an activity has been happening up to now.
why_lv: Present Perfect Continuous rāda, cik ilgi darbība norit līdz šim brīdim.

q: Use the present perfect continuous: She ___ Spanish for six months. (learn)
answers: has been learning
why: *She* + *has been* + verb-ing.
why_lv: *She + has been* + darbības vārds ar *-ing*.

q: Make a question with How long: They have been waiting.
answers: How long have they been waiting?
why: *How long* + *have* + subject + *been* + verb-ing.
why_lv: *How long + have* + teik. priekšmets + *been* + darbības vārds ar *-ing*.

q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct: I have been knowing him for years.
wrong: She has been working here since March.
It has been raining all day.
How long have you been learning English?
why: *Know* is a state verb. We say: *I have known him for years.*
why_lv: *Know* ir stāvokļa darbības vārds. Saka: *I have known him for years.*

q: Your friend is out of breath because she was running until a minute ago. Which sentence explains why?
correct: I've been running.
why: We use the present perfect continuous to explain a present situation by a recent activity.
why_lv: Present Perfect Continuous lieto, lai ar nesenu darbību izskaidrotu situāciju tagad.

q: Write one sentence about something you have been doing a lot lately.
must: Use *have/has been* + verb-ing, for example: *I have been studying a lot.*
Lieto *have/has been* + darbības vārds ar *-ing*, piemēram: *I have been studying a lot.*
model: I have been studying a lot lately.
why: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
why_lv: Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

q: I ___ this book for two weeks, and I'm still reading it.
correct: have been reading
why: An activity that started in the past and is still in progress: *have been* + verb-ing.
why_lv: Darbība, kas sākās pagātnē un joprojām norit: *have been* + darbības vārds ar *-ing*.

q: Which sentence focuses on the result or number (not the activity)?
correct: I've written five emails.
wrong: I've been writing for an hour.
why: Present perfect simple = result or number. Present perfect continuous = the activity and its duration.
why_lv: Present Perfect Simple = rezultāts vai daudzums. Present Perfect Continuous = pati darbība un tās ilgums.

q: Look at the floor! The children ___ with paint. (play)
answers: have been playing
why: A recent activity with a visible result: *have been playing.*
why_lv: Nesena darbība ar redzamu rezultātu: *have been playing*.

q: I ___ this book all week. I ___ three chapters. (read / finish)
answers: have been reading
have finished
why: Activity over time: *have been reading.* Completed result: *have finished.*
why_lv: Darbība laika gaitā: *have been reading*. Pabeigts rezultāts: *have finished*.

q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct: I've been written emails all morning.
wrong: She has been working here since March.
How long have you been living here?
They have been talking for hours.
why: The present perfect continuous uses *have/has been + verb-ing*: *I have been writing emails all morning.* Use *written* in *I have written five emails* to focus on the result.
why_lv: Present Perfect Continuous veido ar *have/has been +* darbības vārdu ar *-ing*: *I have been writing emails all morning.* Formu *written* lieto, piemēram, *I have written five emails*, uzsverot rezultātu.

q: Your boss asks why you look tired. You were in traffic for an hour until now. Choose the correct option.
correct: I've been sitting in traffic for an hour.
wrong: I sit in traffic for an hour.
I will sit in traffic for an hour.
why: A recent, continuing activity that explains the present: present perfect continuous.
why_lv: Nesena, turpinoša darbība, kas izskaidro tagadni: Present Perfect Continuous.

q: Write two sentences: one present perfect continuous about an activity, one present perfect simple about a result.
must: Use *have/has been* + verb-ing in one sentence.
Vienā teikumā lieto *have/has been* + darbības vārds ar *-ing*.
Use *have/has* + past participle in the other sentence.
model: I've been studying all week. I've finished two units.
why: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
why_lv: Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

q: The film began at 7.00. We arrived at 7.15. When we arrived, the film ___ already ___.
correct: had ... started
why: Past perfect = *had* + past participle. It shows an earlier past action.
why_lv: Past Perfect = *had* + 3. forma. Tas rāda agrāku pagātnes darbību.

q: In 'When I got to the station, the train had left', which happened first?
correct: The train left.
wrong: They happened at the same time.
why: The past perfect (*had left*) is the earlier action.
why_lv: Past Perfect (*had left*) ir agrākā darbība.

q: Use the past perfect: She was upset because she ___ her phone. (lose)
answers: had lost
why: The reason came before the feeling: *had* + past participle.
why_lv: Iemesls bija pirms sajūtas: *had* + 3. forma.

q: By the time I called, he ___ out. (already / go)
answers: had already gone
why: *Already* goes between *had* and the past participle: *had already gone.*
why_lv: *Already* iet starp *had* un 3. formu: *had already gone*.

q: Join with After. Use the past perfect for the first action and the past simple for the second: I finished work. Then I went home.
answers: After I had finished work, I went home.
I went home after I had finished work.
why: Here the exercise asks for *After I had finished work, I went home.* In ordinary English, *After I finished work, I went home* is also correct because *after* makes the sequence clear.
why_lv: Šajā uzdevumā jālieto *After I had finished work, I went home.* Ikdienas valodā pareizs ir arī *After I finished work, I went home*, jo *after* skaidri parāda darbību secību.

q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct: When I arrived, she already has left.
wrong: When I arrived, she had already left.
I had never seen snow before that day.
He told me that he had lost his keys.
why: For an earlier past action use *had* + past participle: *she had already left.*
why_lv: Agrākai pagātnes darbībai lieto *had* + 3. forma: *she had already left*.

q: Tom arrived at 9. The meeting started at 8.30. Choose the correct option.
correct: When Tom arrived, the meeting had already started.
wrong: When Tom arrived, the meeting has already started.
When Tom arrived, the meeting would already start.
When Tom arrived, the meeting is already started.
why: The meeting started before Tom arrived, so we use the past perfect for the meeting.
why_lv: Sapulce sākās pirms Toma ierašanās, tāpēc sapulcei lieto Past Perfect.

q: Write one sentence about something that had already happened when you arrived somewhere. Use When I arrived and had already.
must: Use *When I arrived ...* or *By the time ...*
Lieto *When I arrived* ... vai *By the time* ...
model: When I arrived, the film had already started.
why: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
why_lv: Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

q: I am ___ to visit my grandmother tomorrow.
correct: going
why: Plans: *am / is / are + going to* + base verb.
why_lv: Plāniem: *am / is / are + going to* + pamatforma.

q: Which sentence is about the future?
correct: We are going to eat out tonight.
why: *Going to* + base verb talks about a plan for the future.
why_lv: *Going to* + pamatforma runā par plānu nākotnē.

q: Use be going to for a plan: Tom ___ a party on Saturday. (have)
answers: is going to have
why: A plan: *is going to* + base verb.
hints: After *going to* we use the base verb: *have*, not *has.*
why_lv: Plāns: *is going to* + pamatforma.

q: It's cold. I ___ my coat. (take)
answers: 'll take
will take
'm going to take
am going to take
why: A quick decision now: *will* + base verb.
why_lv: Ātrs lēmums tagad: *will* + pamatforma.

q: Make a question: You are going to travel by train.
answers: Are you going to travel by train?
why: Question: *Are* + *you* + *going to* + base verb?
why_lv: Jautājums: *Are + you + going to* + pamatforma?

q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct: I going to buy a bike.
why: We need *am / is / are* before *going to*: *I am going to buy a bike.*
why_lv: Pirms *going to* vajag *am / is / are*: *I am going to buy a bike.*

q: A friend asks: 'What are you going to do at the weekend?' Choose the correct option.
correct: I'm going to visit my parents.
wrong: I visit my parents every day.
why: The question is about a future plan, so we answer with *going to.*
why_lv: Jautājums ir par nākotnes plānu, tāpēc atbild ar *going to*.

q: Write one sentence about your plan for tomorrow. Use I am going to.
must: Use *I am going to* + base verb, for example: *I'm going to visit a friend.*
Lieto *I am going to* + pamatforma, piemēram: *I'm going to visit a friend.*
model: I'm going to visit a friend tomorrow.
why: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
why_lv: Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

q: Look at those clouds! It ___ rain.
correct: is going to
why: *Going to* is used for predictions based on what we can see now: *is going to* + base verb.
why_lv: *Going to* lieto prognozēm, kas balstītas uz to, ko redzam tagad: *is going to* + pamatforma.

q: Which sentence is a plan we made before now?
correct: I'm going to start a new course in March.
wrong: I think prices will go up.
why: *Going to* shows a plan or intention made before speaking.
why_lv: *Going to* rāda plānu vai nodomu, kas radies pirms runāšanas.

q: The phone is ringing. - I ___ it. (answer)
answers: 'll answer
will answer
why: A decision at the moment of speaking: *will* + base verb.
why_lv: Lēmums runāšanas brīdī: *will* + pamatforma.

q: We ___ to Rome next month. We've already bought the tickets. (go)
answers: are going
are going to go
why: A plan already arranged: *are going (to)*.
why_lv: Jau sarunāts plāns: *are going* (*to*).

q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct: I will to help you.
wrong: I'm going to visit my aunt next week.
She is going to have a baby.
why: After *will* we use the base verb without *to*: *I will help you.*
why_lv: Pēc *will* lieto pamatformu bez *to*: *I will help you.*

q: You see dark clouds. Which sentence is a prediction from what you can see now?
correct: It's going to rain.
why: *It is going to rain* highlights evidence visible now. *It will rain* is also a possible prediction, but does not highlight that evidence as directly.

This is a possible prediction. Here *going to* highlights the visible evidence more directly.
The present simple normally describes a general pattern here, not this evidence-based prediction.
This describes past rain, not the future rain you are predicting.

why_lv: *It is going to rain* uzsver tagad redzamās pazīmes. Arī *It will rain* var izteikt prognozi, bet neuzsver redzamo pamatojumu tik tieši.

Tā ir iespējama prognoze. Šajā situācijā *going to* tiešāk uzsver redzamās pazīmes.
Present Simple šeit parasti apraksta vispārīgu parādību, nevis šo uz redzamām pazīmēm balstīto prognozi.
Tas apraksta lietu pagātnē, nevis prognozēto lietu nākotnē.

q: Write a sentence about your plan for next weekend. Use going to.
model: I'm going to visit my parents next weekend.
why: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
why_lv: Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

q: If it ___ tomorrow, we will stay at home.
correct: rains
why: After *if, when* and *as soon as* we use the present simple for the future.
why_lv: Pēc *if, when* un *as soon as* nākotnei lieto Present Simple.

q: Which sentence is an arrangement (fixed time and place in your diary)?
correct: I'm seeing the dentist at 3 pm on Friday.
wrong: I will probably see the dentist.
why: The present continuous with a time shows a fixed arrangement.
why_lv: Present Continuous ar laiku rāda fiksētu vienošanos.

q: I'll call you when I ___ home. (get)
answers: get
why: After *when* we use the present simple, not *will.*
hints: After *when* we use the present simple: *when I get home.*
Pēc *when* lieto Present Simple: *when I get home*.
why_lv: Pēc *when* lieto Present Simple, nevis *will*.

q: Wait! I ___ you with that bag. (help)
answers: 'll help
will help
why: An offer at the moment of speaking: *will* + base verb.
why_lv: Piedāvājums runāšanas brīdī: *will* + pamatforma.

q: Rewrite with going to: I plan to buy a car.
answers: I'm going to buy a car.
I am going to buy a car.
why: *Going to* shows a plan: *am going to* + base verb.
why_lv: *Going to* rāda plānu: *am going to* + pamatforma.

q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct: I'll call you when I will arrive.
wrong: We're flying to Rome on Monday.
I think it'll be a great trip.
As soon as he arrives, we will start.
why: In time clauses (*when, as soon as, before*) use the present simple: *when I arrive.*
why_lv: Laika palīgteikumos (*when, as soon as, before*) lieto Present Simple: *when I arrive*.

q: Your friend says: 'I will meet Anna at 6, we agreed yesterday.' Choose the more natural option for an arrangement.
correct: I'm meeting Anna at 6.
wrong: I'm going to be met Anna at 6.
why: For arrangements with a time we often use the present continuous.
why_lv: Vienošanās ar laiku bieži izsaka ar Present Continuous.

q: Write a sentence with when or as soon as about what you will do after class or work.
must: Use *when, as soon as, after* or *before.*
Lieto *when, as soon as, after* vai *before*.
Use *will* or *going to* for the later action.
model: As soon as I finish work, I'll go to the gym.
why: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
why_lv: Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

q: Hurry up! The film ___ to start.
correct: is about
why: *Be about to* + base verb = very soon.
why_lv: *Be about to* + pamatforma = pavisam drīz.

q: Which sentence means something will happen very soon?
correct: The plane is about to take off.
wrong: The plane takes off every day.
The plane has been taking off.
why: *Be about to* is used for the very near future.
why_lv: *Be about to* lieto pavisam tuvai nākotnei.

q: Make a promise with will: Don't worry. I ___ anyone your secret. (not / tell)
answers: won't tell
will not tell
why: A promise: *will / won't* + base verb.
why_lv: Solījums: *will / won't* + pamatforma.

q: Use be going to for a prediction based on what you see: Be careful! You ___ off that chair! (fall)
answers: are going to fall
why: We can see it is about to happen: *are going to* + base verb.
why_lv: Redzam, ka tūlīt notiks: *are going to* + pamatforma.

q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct: He is going to be arrive soon.
wrong: It's going to rain; look at the sky.
why: After *going to* we use the base verb: *He is going to arrive soon.*
why_lv: Pēc *going to* lieto pamatformu: *He is going to arrive soon.*

q: You see a colleague with heavy boxes. Choose the correct option.
correct: I'll carry one of those for you.
wrong: I carry one of those for you.
I'm carrying one of those for you.
I carried one of those for you.
why: *Will* is the natural choice for a spontaneous offer.
why_lv: Spontānam piedāvājumam dabiskākais ir *will*.

q: Write two sentences: one prediction with going to (with a reason) and one spontaneous offer with will.
must: Use *going to* + base verb in the prediction.
Use *I'll* or *I will* for the offer.
model: It's going to rain; look at the clouds. I'll bring an umbrella for you.
why: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
why_lv: Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

q: English ___ in many countries.
correct: is spoken
why: Passive = *be* + past participle. *English* is singular, so *is spoken.*
why_lv: Ciešamā kārta = *be* + 3. forma. *English* ir vienskaitlī, tāpēc *is spoken*.

q: Which sentence is passive?
correct: Rice is grown in Asia.
why: In a passive sentence the thing that receives the action is the subject: *Rice is grown.*
why_lv: Ciešamās kārtas teikumā teikuma priekšmets ir tas, kas saņem darbību: *Rice is grown.*

q: Bread ___ from flour. (make)
answers: is made
why: Passive present simple: *is/are* + past participle. *Bread* = *it.*
why_lv: Ciešamā kārta, Present Simple: *is/are* + 3. forma. *Bread = it.*

q: These cars ___ in Germany. (build)
answers: are built
why: *These cars* = *they*, so *are built.*
why_lv: *These cars = they*, tāpēc *are built*.

q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct: Coffee is grow in Brazil.
wrong: The shops are closed on Sunday.
why: The passive needs the past participle: *Coffee is grown in Brazil.*
why_lv: Ciešamajai kārtai vajag 3. formu: *Coffee is grown in Brazil.*

q: Why do we say 'Tickets are sold here'?
correct: The action is important. We don't need to say who sells them.
wrong: Because the tickets are very old.
Because we want to say who sells them.
Because the sentence is in the past.

*Unless* jau nozīmē *if ... not*, tāpēc darbības vārds aiz tā parasti ir apgalvojošā formā: *Unless you practise*, ...
why_lv: *Unless* nozīmē *if ... not*, tāpēc teikums aiz tā parasti ir apgalvojošs: *Unless you practise, you won't improve.*

q: Which sentence means the same as: 'If you don't hurry, you will be late.'?

If you send us the documents today, we would process your request by Friday.
why: Real future condition: *if* + present simple, *will* + base verb.
why_lv: Reāls nākotnes nosacījums: *if* + Present Simple, *will* + pamatforma.

q: Write a sentence with in case (for example: I'll take an umbrella in case it rains). Use the present simple after in case.

why: Compare your sentence with the model answer.

q: Choose the correct form: If I ___ a million euros, I would buy a boat.

why_lv: Second conditional: *if* + Past Simple, *would* + pamatforma.

correct: I am not tall, so I don't play basketball.
wrong: I am tall and I play basketball.
I played basketball when I was young.

why_lv: Second conditional runā par nereālām vai maz ticamām situācijām. Darbības vārds ir pagātnē, bet nozīme ir par tagadni.

q: If I ___ the boss, I ___ cancel all Monday meetings. (be)
answers: were
was
would
'd
why: Second conditional: *if* + past simple (*were*), *would* + base verb.
why_lv: Second conditional: *if* + Past Simple (*were*), *would* + pamatforma.

If I were you, I wouldn't do that.
What would you do if you saw a ghost?
why: The if-part uses the past simple, not *will*: *If I won the lottery, ...*
why_lv: *If* daļā lieto Past Simple, nevis *will*: *If I won the lottery*, ...

q: Your friend can't decide whether to quit and become a baker. You give advice. Choose the correct option.

If I would be you, I talk to a few bakers first.
If I was you, I will talk to a few bakers first.

why_lv: Padomam saka: *If I were you, I would* + pamatforma.

why: Second conditional question: *What would you do if you* + past simple?
why_lv: Second conditional jautājums: *What would you do if you* + Past Simple?

If you heat ice, it melts.
This is always true.

why_lv: Zero: vienmēr patiess. First: reāla nākotne. Second: nereāls tagad. Third: nereāls pagātnē.

why_lv: Second conditional: *if* + Past Simple, *would / could* + pamatforma.
